history.origins: 1000 (Tysiacha/Tysiąc) is a point-trick marriage game well known across Eastern Europe—Russia, Belarus, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Poland, and Lithuania. In Russian it is Tysiacha (Тысяча), in Polish Tysiąc; both mean 'thousand,' the target score. Slight rule variations exist between and within countries; the Polish form Tysiąc licytowany (Auction 1000) is widely played as Poland's national card game.
timeline: 20th century: widely played as Poland's national marriage and trick-taking game.

rules.objective: Be the first to reach 1000 points by winning the auction, taking the talon, and scoring at least your bid from card points and marriage declarations; opponents score from their own tricks.
rules.gameplay: Auction: bid points you'll score (min 100). Winner takes musik, discards 2. Marriages (K+Q same suit): â™¥=100, â™¦=80, â™£=60, â™ =40. Declaring marriage = that suit becomes trump. Follow suit, must trump if void. A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2. 120 card points total. Bomb option to avoid setback.

variations.noVariationsReason: Sources describe the standard three-player auction form; regional and optional rules (e.g. Polish Tysiąc, two-player, barrel) are documented but not listed as separate variations.

difficulty.easy: Basic bidding without marriage anticipation; plays cards randomly.
difficulty.medium: Tracks marriages and manages musician cards; moderate bid strategy.
difficulty.hard: Perfect marriage tracking, optimal bidding, manages bomb and 900+ endgame.

phases.label: Deal
phases.notes: Deal 7 cards to each player and 3 to talon (prikup).

phases.label: Bidding
phases.notes: Auction: minimum 100, multiples of 5 or 10. Two passes end bidding.

phases.label: Exchange
phases.notes: Declarer takes talon, then passes one card face down to each opponent; all have 8 cards.

phases.label: Play
phases.notes: Declarer leads first. Follow suit; must trump if void. After winning a trick, may declare marriage (K+Q) to set trump.

pass.description: Pass in the auction; a player who has passed cannot bid again in that round.
pass.constraints: Legal during bidding when it is your turn to bid.

bid.description: Bid the number of points you undertake to score; minimum 100, bids in multiples of 5 or 10. Highest bidder becomes declarer and takes the talon.
bid.constraints: Legal during bidding phase; must bid at least 100; must bid higher than previous or pass; to bid over 120 you must hold at least one king-queen pair.

meld.description: Declare a marriage (King and Queen of same suit); scores bonus points (Hearts 100, Diamonds 80, Clubs 60, Spades 40) and sets that suit as trump. Must lead one of the pair to the next trick.
meld.constraints: Legal only immediately after winning a trick; must hold both K and Q of a suit and lead one of them.

go_out.reason: This game has no go-out action.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Trump beats plain suit; must follow suit, must trump if void.

meldConfig.initialMeldRequirement: King and Queen of same suit; declaring sets that suit as trump.

customActions.description: Deal 7 cards to each active player and 3 cards face down to the centre (talon/prikup/musik).
customActions.constraints: Performed by dealer at start of each hand.

customActions.description: Take the three talon cards into hand, then pass one card face down to each opponent so everyone has 8 cards. Declarer may then raise the bid.
customActions.constraints: Only the auction winner (declarer) performs this after bidding ends.

engine.handRankingSystem: Point-trick: no hand rankings; card points A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2, 9=0; marriage bonuses by suit.
engine.rankingSystem: A 10 K Q J 9 in each suit; trump beats plain.
engine.deckDescription: A heavily stripped French deck containing 24 cards with four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) and six ranks per suit (9 through Ace), created by removing all 2s through 8s from a standard 52-card deck.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card design and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Six ranks per suit in ascending order: 9, 10, Jack (Valet), Queen (Dame), King (Roi), and Ace as the highest card, where each rank determines card strength and trick-winning potential in various games.
engine.dealPattern: 7 each, 3 to talon (prikup); after exchange everyone has 8.
